16:I[12454,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0otjhi71vbmnx.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0j1uy9t~zxcf0.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/1304s0wcp2kce.js"],"WeeklyView"]
17:T47a,The authors build a controlled pretraining setup using a Fictional Knowledge Dataset with 2,048 synthetic facts about invented entities and attributes. Each fact is rendered into diverse documents across languages for injection during pretraining, with held-out multiple-choice questions for evaluation. For a fact, the authors know exactly how many times it appeared in language A and language B. They then regress target-language accuracy on native and foreign exposure counts. The ratio between the foreign-exposure coefficient and the native-exposure coefficient defines CL_eq. A score of 100% means that one exposure in the foreign language is as useful as one exposure in the target language; 0% means no effective transfer. To remove natural-language confounds, the paper also evaluates cloned language copies that are structurally identical but occupy different token spaces. This isolates vocabulary separation from syntax or semantics. The main intervention, word-wise translation, is motivated by this mechanism: it tries to unify token spaces for otherwise vocabulary-disjoint languages rather than relying on post-training alignment.18:T426,The experiments pretrain bilingual models from scratch while injecting fictional facts at controlled rates. Two scales are used: a 360M-parameter SmolLM2-style model and a 7B-parameter Llama-3 adaptation, both with a 65,536-token BPE vocabulary. The dataset validation shows chance-level MCQ accuracy with zero injection and a roughly log-shaped improvement as injected paraphrases increase, confirming that the facts are learnable and exposure-controlled. The main measurements show that compartmentalization already appears during pretraining. Disjoint token spaces strongly reduce cross-lingual transfer, and this effect persists across model scales. The authors also replicate key checks with a fictive-persona dataset built around high-frequency human names, reducing the chance that the result is only about rare synthetic entity tokens. The word-wise translation intervention improves both CL_eq and language-modeling perplexity, which supports the claim that token-space unification improves the training signal rather than only the diagnostic benchmark.19:T441,QVAC Genesis III contains 191.43B synthetic STEM tokens across 19 domains and three difficulty levels, rendered in four styles: textbook, web article, QA, and dialogue. The pipeline samples seed passages from FineFineWeb, filters them with the Ultra-FineWeb quality classifier, and keeps roughly 500k high-quality seeds. QwQ-32B is then used to generate self-contained multiple-choice questions. A weak edge-scale student answers the questions, and an answer-extraction step decides whether the student matches the gold label. Wrong answers trigger a Failure Analysis pipeline, where a teacher model diagnoses the misconception and writes a targeted corrective explanation. Correct answers trigger an Option-Level reasoning pipeline, where the teacher explains the correct option and each distractor. This differs from standard synthetic textbook generation because the student response controls the form of supervision. The paper also introduces an LLM-as-a-parser evaluation protocol that extracts final answers from free-form generations and reports both accuracy and Valid Answer Rate.1a:T4c8,The method starts from the geometry of the prediction-loss and predictive-entropy plane. A likelihood-only detector uses a horizontal threshold on loss. This fails when many non-members have low loss because they are predictable. The proposed detector instead uses an inclined boundary by correcting loss with predictive entropy. The resulting score has the algebraic form of Helmholtz free energy: token loss plays the role of an energy term, predictive entropy is the uncertainty term, and a coefficient similar to temperature trades them off, giving a score of the form loss minus an entropy correction before sequence-level aggregation. The theoretical analysis shows that when members and non-members have the same mean predictive entropy, the correction preserves the expected membership gap and its lower bound. When the loss gap and entropy gap are positively correlated, an appropriate correction reduces the variance of the gap while preserving its mean, improving standardized separation. The analysis is also extended to settings with a nonzero mean entropy gap. Compared with reference-model or perturbation-based calibration, ETD uses the target model’s own token-level predictive distribution more directly.1b:T485,The technical contribution is a clean training framework rather than a new architecture. The paper keeps architecture, model size, tokenizer, and overall language mixture fixed, while varying two main factors: the L1 identity and the order in which the two languages are presented during pretraining. English is always the L2, and the suite spans 21 L1s. The authors train under five exposure regimes, covering more interleaved versus more staged curricula, at three FineWeb scales: 100M, 2B, and 24B tokens, plus a human-scale 100M condition. A strong design choice is the inclusion of matched monolingual baselines for 20 languages, which helps separate genuine bilingual transfer from simple data-composition effects. Conceptually, the framework unifies structured exposure and sequential bilingual training ideas from earlier work, but treats exposure timing itself as the primary intervention. Evaluation is also broader than perplexity: the main target is psycholinguistic alignment, especially L2 eye-tracking reading times on MECO, with additional probes on cross-lingual structural priming and CEFR-stratified learner-error discrimination on BLiSS.1c:T4d9,The most consistent result is that ordered or staged exposure tends to align better with human L2 reading times than fully interleaved training. The paper argues this effect is not explained away by higher overall proficiency or better language balance, which is important because those are the obvious confounds. In other words, the point in training when a language is introduced appears to be a meaningful determinant of human-like L2 processing behavior. A second important finding is that the curriculum effect does not transfer uniformly across tasks. On structural priming and BLiSS learner-error discrimination, balanced exposure is often competitive or even better. So staged curricula seem to shape specific processing dynamics rather than universally improving bilingual competence. In scale terms, the suite includes 285 bilingual and 45 monolingual models across 100M, 2B, and 24B tokens, all with checkpoint trajectories. The paper also compares against larger massively multilingual models and reports that carefully designed bilingual curricula can match or exceed their L2 reading-time alignment under much smaller parameter budgets. For researchers working on scaling and data curricula, that is the most actionable result.1d:T424,Read this as an experimental-design paper. Start with the setup sections and verify exactly what is held fixed and what is varied; that is where the credibility of the later claims comes from. Then focus on the exposure-regime definitions, data-scale settings, construction of matched monolingual baselines, and checkpoint release strategy. In the experiments, prioritize the MECO reading-time analysis, since that is the main empirical claim. Pay attention to how the authors rule out alternative explanations such as proficiency and balance. After that, read the structural priming and BLiSS sections to understand where the curriculum effect does and does not generalize. The most useful deeper questions are: whether exposure schedule should be treated as an independent scaling axis, whether early checkpoints reveal transfer-emergence phases, and whether matched monolingual controls can be imported into broader multilingual or continual-pretraining studies. A skim takes about 25–35 minutes; the figures and appendix are where much of the value sits.1e:T42e,The method is a parallel agentic search loop. Human scientists provide a high-level prompt asking Claude to search DNA sequence databases for interesting reverse transcriptase examples. Claude reads the relevant literature, reproduces established results on public data to check its methods, searches protein families and genomic neighborhoods for systems that do not match known categories, and writes short reports for candidates with proposed functions and supporting evidence. Follow-up Claude sessions critique the evidence and eliminate many weak candidates. Human scientists then review the survivors and test them in the lab. The important design choice is not asking the model for a direct answer. The workflow decomposes discovery into literature calibration, database search, anomaly detection, candidate reporting, self-critique, expert filtering, and biochemical follow-up. The team also studies the model’s generated hypotheses as data, comparing candidates that experts keep against those they discard, then feeding those lessons back into instructions.1f:T57b,A BDLM splits a length-L sequence into B contiguous blocks of size M=L/B. Blocks are generated left to right, while tokens inside a block are denoised in parallel. During training, each target block b is corrupted at a sampled diffusion time and denoised conditioned on the clean prefix x(<b). The total objective is a sum over per-block losses. The paper exploits this structure. In conventional implementations, training builds a length-2L representation containing a clean copy and a corrupted copy, then applies a block-causal attention mask. Under context parallelism, both clean and corrupted K/V are sharded and communicated. The mismatch is that clean prefixes are shared by many later blocks, while corrupted K/V are local to one block. Block parallelism assigns each complete corrupted-block computation to a rank, keeping that block’s corrupted Q/K/V, activations, and gradients local. This removes block-specific cross-rank communication. The drawback is replication of long overlapping clean prefixes. Context-sharded block parallelism fixes this by sharding the clean sequence across the same ranks: each rank owns clean K/V shards that can serve all local block computations whose prefixes include those shards, and backward contributions are accumulated at the shard owner. The result preserves local corrupted-block computation while distributing clean-prefix storage and computation.20:T49d,The reported results are organized around four operational questions. First, CPT does acquire new knowledge. The effect is strongest for OLMo2 and Gemma-3 1B, while the Llama-family gains are smaller. On pre-cutoff questions, five of six models also improve, which argues against broad factual forgetting. Gains are larger for more recent events and persist even when the source articles are not in the training corpus, reducing the likelihood that the result is only direct memorization. Second, the cost to general capability is small: macro-averaged accuracy over 13 downstream tasks stays within 0.01 of the base model for every model, and 11 of the 13 tasks remain within ±0.02. Third, the training recipe shows clear tradeoffs. A curated 6B-token slice captures most of the available signal; one learning rate cannot jointly optimize new-knowledge acquisition and general benchmark retention; sufficiently high-rank LoRA matches full CPT with much lower memory; and performance plateaus within roughly the first third of training. Fourth, CPT gains survive SFT, but DPO is model-family dependent: it partially erodes gains for Llama-3.1 8B while improving them for OLMo2 7B.21:T450,Terminal Shrinkage Averaging returns an interpolation between the last checkpoint and the mean of the last K checkpoints: (1-α)θ_T + α\bar{θ}_T. α=0 recovers the raw final iterate, and α=1 recovers uniform LAWA. Since the final checkpoint is included in the average, its total weight is 1-α+α/K, while each earlier checkpoint receives α/K. The analysis uses a local quadratic approximation to the loss over the short terminal region. Checkpoints are decomposed into their across-run mean and stochastic residuals, and risk is measured in the Hessian-induced seminorm. Under this model, the expected surrogate risk is quadratic in α. The expression exposes the tradeoff: averaging older checkpoints can move the mean away from the local optimum, but it can also reduce stochastic terminal variation. This gives conditions where the best α lies strictly between raw final iterate and full LAWA. The same framework explains why an averaged estimator can prefer a higher terminal learning-rate floor: the trajectory keeps making progress late in training, while the estimator damps endpoint noise.22:T432,The experiments are designed around the interaction rather than only the main effects. Depth-12 NanoChat runs first show that the best shrinkage coefficient is inside the interval, not at α=0 or α=1. A paired factorial experiment then crosses terminal learning-rate floors of 5%, 10%, and 15% of peak LR with two output estimators, raw final iterate and TSA, using five repetitions. Increasing the floor worsens validation BPB when deploying the raw endpoint, but improves validation BPB when deploying TSA; the effect grows as the floor is raised. A replication with pure AdamW preserves the direction of the interaction, so the result is not tied to the Muon+AdamW optimizer mix used in NanoChat. The higher-floor-plus-TSA recipe is also applied to a depth-22 NanoChat time-to-GPT-2 setting, where it improves over the public recipe at matched budget and yields a qualifying benchmark run. The provided material does not include the exact BPB table, so the reliable quantitative details are the floor values, repetition count, model depths, and direction of the effects.23:T845,方法核心是把某个前缀 h 处的一次局部梯度贡献写成随机变量 Z_h，并对其总方差做 law-of-total-variance 分解。分解后有两部分：第一部分是 decision uncertainty，即在前缀 h 上，不同动作 a 的 score function 与 Q_h(a) 组合后带来的方差；第二部分是 continuation uncertainty，即动作已经选定后，后续随机 suffix 带来的回报噪声。这个分解直接对应两种算力操作：新增 branch 用来降低 decision uncertainty；对已有 branch 做更多 suffix resampling，用来降低 continuation uncertainty。

在此基础上，作者推导了两个分配规律。其一是 compute-optimal suffix allocation law：给定某个前缀和动作，suffix rollout 数应按该动作的 continuation variance 与单位成本来分配，而不是平均分。其二是 marginal branching law：是否在某个前缀继续加一个新分支，取决于该前缀的 occupancy、score-weighted value uncertainty，以及新增分支的预期信息增益相对计算成本的比值。作者把这个量具体化为 EPIG，expected predictive information gain about the gradient。直观上，它不是问“这里模型是否犹豫”，而是问“如果我在这里多看一个分支，能否显著减少我对梯度方向的未知”。

算法层面，EPIG-Tree 不是完全抛弃 entropy。它先用 entropy 作为 proposal mechanism，筛出可能值得分叉的候选节点，因为低熵节点往往没有有效分歧；然后再用 EPIG 进行真正的算力分配，决定哪些节点值得扩展、哪些节点只需补 suffix、哪些节点不值得继续投入。这样做的原因很实际：直接精确评估所有节点的梯度信息增益代价太高，而 entropy 作为候选筛选器便宜且能排除大量无效位置。与 TreeRL/EPTree、TreePO 这类方法相比，区别不在“是否用树”，而在“树的生长目标函数”。已有方法更偏向局部不确定性或段级建模；这篇工作把目标直接对准梯度估计误差，并把 branch 与 suffix allocation 统一到同一方差框架里。24:T773,The core setup defines the local gradient contribution at a prefix h as a random variable Z_h and decomposes its variance via the law of total variance. This yields two distinct sources of estimator error. The first is decision uncertainty: variance induced by which action a is taken at prefix h, weighted by the score function and the action value Q_h(a). The second is continuation uncertainty: variance in the suffix return after the action has already been fixed. This decomposition maps cleanly to two compute operations. Adding a new branch reduces decision uncertainty. Adding more suffix rollouts under an existing branch reduces continuation uncertainty.

From this view, the paper derives two allocation laws. First, a compute-optimal suffix allocation law: suffix samples should be distributed according to continuation variance and cost, rather than uniformly across branches. Second, a marginal branching law: whether to add another branch at a prefix depends on occupancy, score-weighted value uncertainty, and the expected reduction in gradient-estimation error relative to compute cost. The operational quantity is EPIG, expected predictive information gain about the gradient. The key distinction is that entropy only measures whether branches can differ, while EPIG measures whether those differences matter for the gradient estimator.

Algorithmically, EPIG-Tree still uses entropy, but only as a proposal mechanism. Entropy cheaply filters candidate branching points, while EPIG decides where compute is actually spent. This is a practical compromise: exact information-gain evaluation everywhere would be too expensive. Compared with prior tree-based LLM RL methods such as entropy-triggered branching or segment-level tree modeling, the novelty is the objective function. The tree is optimized for gradient estimation quality, not for uncertainty alone or for generic search coverage.25:T64d,The empirical section spans four settings designed to validate the theory rather than only show end-task gains. First, cloned-state continuous control provides a controlled environment for testing the branching and suffix-allocation laws. Second, frozen LLM gradient calibration directly measures how well different tree construction strategies approximate the target gradient; this is one of the most important experiments because it matches the paper’s stated objective. Third, single-turn LLM math evaluates whether EPIG-Tree improves compute efficiency under verifiable rewards. Fourth, online multi-turn Wordle tests the method in a setting with recovery behavior, sequential dependence, and environment stochasticity.

The reported pattern is consistent across the paper: EPIG-Tree helps most when continuation noise is substantial and when only a small subset of decisions materially affects the final outcome. In those regimes, independent rollouts and entropy-only branching waste budget on low-value variation. The paper is also careful about boundary conditions. When the environment is nearly deterministic, trajectories are short, or entropy already aligns well with value-relevant branching, cheaper entropy baselines can match or nearly match EPIG-Tree. That is an important result because it clarifies where the extra machinery is justified. The provided text does not include the full numeric tables, so it is better to avoid inventing exact deltas; the main reported metrics are gradient calibration error, return under fixed compute budgets, and performance curves as branching budget varies.26:T4ea,If time is limited, focus on the introduction, the variance decomposition proposition, the EPIG definition and allocation algorithm, and the frozen-LLM calibration plus Wordle experiments. The conceptual center of the paper is not “tree rollouts” by itself, but the claim that a rollout tree is an experimental device for estimating policy gradients. While reading, track three questions. First, which quantities in the decomposition are directly estimable and which require approximation? Second, how is EPIG computed cheaply enough to be useful online? Third, why is entropy a good proposal signal but a poor final allocation criterion?

Two parts are especially worth deeper inspection. One is occupancy weighting: in language-model training, high-frequency prefixes and rare prefixes do not contribute equally to the gradient, and this changes the branching objective. The other is the suffix allocation law, which suggests possible links to adaptive compute, verifier-guided rollouts, and speculative branching. To judge practical scalability, pay attention to algorithmic complexity, parallel implementation details, and whether the method assumes cloned states or reversible environments in ways that may limit deployment in large-scale online RL.27:T43d,The strongest evidence comes from ARC-AGI-3, Frontier-CS polyomino packing, MNIST classifier compression, and Terminal-Bench 2.0. On ARC-AGI-3 with Claude Sonnet 4.6, team@3 matches roughly best@13, and team@5 matches roughly best@33, corresponding to effective multipliers of about 4.3x and 6.6x independent agents. On FT09, single-agent success is 9.4%, while team@3 reaches 90%. On LP85, 64 single-agent trials fail to solve the game, while team@5 succeeds 65% of the time. The negative result on Terminal-Bench 2.0 is important: team@2 improves over one attempt but does not beat independent pass@2, likely because intermediate feedback is not reliable enough to rank partial solutions.28:T7dd,Hill Sampling is intentionally minimal. Start from an initial program x0. At each round, sample N candidate edits from a frozen LLM conditioned on the current incumbent xt. Execute each candidate with the verifier, obtain rewards, and replace the incumbent if the best candidate in the round matches or exceeds the best reward seen so far. The algorithm stores the incumbent’s historical best reward rather than re-evaluating it every round, which is important when execution is stochastic. Equal-reward replacements are allowed to preserve some structural diversity. There is no archive, no crossover, no explicit diversity objective, and no parameter update. The main knobs are decoding temperature, samples per round, and number of rounds.

The paper is stronger because it does not stop at introducing the method. It systematically compares three exploration families. First, repeated sampling, where all generations are drawn independently from the same starting point. Relative to that baseline, Hill Sampling adds exactly one persistent state: the best-so-far program fed back into context. Second, evolution strategies applied directly to LLM weights. The authors build a large-scale ES pipeline and separate standard ES learning from a zero-learning-rate variant that keeps only random weight perturbations. This isolates exploration from learning. Third, they test common add-ons such as diversity encouragement, solution combination, extra exploration mechanisms, and code-execution feedback. The conclusion is that none of these are necessary to obtain strong results in this setting.

Mechanistically, Hill Sampling treats the LLM as a conditional editor rather than a one-shot generator. The incumbent acts as a moving scaffold. Future samples are drawn near the current best program instead of restarting from the original problem statement. That creates a simple local search process in context space, not in parameter space. The paper’s main contribution is showing how far that alone can go.29:T79c,The evaluation covers three verifiable mathematical optimization problems with three open-weight models: circle packing with gpt-oss-20b, sums/differences of finite sets with OLMo-3.1-32B-Instruct, and Erdős’ minimum-overlap problem with Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct. The emphasis is practical wall-clock performance, not only sample efficiency.

The headline result is on circle packing: Hill Sampling reaches the best published result in under five hours on eight H100 GPUs. On the Erdős minimum-overlap problem, it surpasses the AlphaEvolve algorithmic-discovery reference within 12 hours. The abstract is truncated, but the body makes the qualitative outcome clear: one new published best result and strong competitive performance on the other tasks.

The ablations are the most informative part. Hill Sampling substantially outperforms repeated sampling, showing that best-so-far conditioning is the main source of gain. Standard ES often improves mean return while reducing maximum return, which directly supports the paper’s framing that mean-oriented updates can be misaligned with discovery objectives. Setting the ES learning rate to zero removes learning but keeps random weight perturbations; this sometimes preserves maximum return better than learned ES, yet still underperforms plain token-sampling randomness from the unperturbed model. That is a useful boundary condition for claims about nearby experts in pretrained weight space: even if such experts exist, searching for them may be less effective than output-space exploration when exact verification is available.

The paper also compares Hill Sampling with N=64 and N=512 under the same total sampling budget, changing the trade-off between more frequent incumbent updates and larger within-round candidate sets. Even without all table values here, the setup is worth attention because it probes whether iterative conditioning matters more than wider one-shot search.2a:T514,For a quick read, focus on three parts. That distinction has direct implications for verifier-guided decoding, best-of-N methods, and some RL-style test-time adaptation setups.2b:T867,方法核心有四部分。第一，模型骨架仍是 Qwen3 causal backbone，作者没有改成双向注意力，而是保留 causal mask。这样做的直接好处是天然兼容 KV cache，也能继承成熟 AR 模型的训练稳定性；代价是 diffusion 目标不能做标准的全双向 masked denoising，只能做 causal masked reconstruction。第二，引入 slot 化训练。目标序列被切成连续的固定长度 slot，每个样本随机采样一个 p_mask，决定有多少 slot 被整体 mask。未 mask 的 slot 走 AR next-token loss，mask 的 slot 全部替换成特殊的 <mdm_mask>，走重建 loss。于是同一次前向里，模型同时学“在可见局部里顺序预测”和“在给定上下文下恢复整段缺失内容”。第三，作者对输入顺序做了专门重排：clean slots 放在前，masked slots 放在后，同时 clean/masked 两组内部还可打乱顺序。这个设计的关键不是数据花样，而是让 masked 部分在 causal attention 下仍能看到全部 visible prefix，从而在不破坏因果掩码的前提下模拟一种条件去噪。第四，slot size curriculum。训练初期 slot 很小，例如从 2 开始，后续逐步扩到 4、8、16、32、64。小 slot 时，masked reconstruction 更接近局部补全，优化难度低；slot 变大后，模型必须在更粗粒度上恢复长片段，逐渐学习更强的并行补全能力。文中还加入 ordered_sampling，使 slot 内 token 的 mask 强度从左到右递增，并通过 1/p_mask 的归一化加权，让模型更重视 slot 起始 token 的正确预测，因为这些 token 会决定后续整段生成的走向。另一些实现细节如 grouped_noise、max_span_length、noise_sorting，则是为了统一支持 prefix completion、fill-in-the-prefix、fill-in-the-middle 和随机 span masking 等不同缺失模式。与 BD3-LMs 相比，Zarya 不把 block size 固定死；与 Eso-LMs 相比，它不是只在 loss 层面混合，而是把训练样本结构、mask 机制和 curriculum 一起设计；与 ReFusion 相比，它更强调训练—推理解耦，同一模型可切换双模式推理。2c:T432,Its value for pretraining research is threefold. First, it offers a practical route for non-pure-AR language modeling that does not require abandoning a causal backbone. That matters because many alternatives to AR become difficult to integrate into existing training and serving stacks. Second, Zarya explicitly decouples training configuration from inference mode. A trained model can be used either with MDM-style sampling or with slotted speculative decoding through an inference flag, which is more flexible than methods whose training setup hard-codes the decoding regime. Third, the slot curriculum is interesting as a training-dynamics device, not just as data formatting. Small slots keep the task close to AR and easier to optimize; larger slots force broader reconstruction and more parallel behavior. At this stage, the contribution looks more like a promising modeling recipe than a definitive replacement for standard large-scale AR pretraining.2d:T84c,The method has four main components. First, the backbone remains a causal Qwen3 model. The authors do not switch to bidirectional attention. This preserves KV-cache compatibility and leverages the optimization stability of standard AR models, but it also means the diffusion objective cannot be a fully bidirectional masked denoising objective. Instead, Zarya uses a causal masked-reconstruction objective. Second, the target sequence is partitioned into contiguous fixed-length slots. For each example, a mask ratio p_mask is sampled, and a subset of slots is fully masked. Visible slots contribute an autoregressive next-token loss, while masked slots are replaced by a special <mdm_mask> token and contribute a reconstruction loss. The model therefore learns sequential prediction and context-conditioned parallel recovery within the same forward pass. Third, the input is reordered so that clean slots come before masked slots, and both groups may be permuted internally. This is a key design choice: under causal attention, masked positions can still attend to the visible prefix, which gives a denoising-like conditional structure without breaking causal masking or KV-cache reuse. Fourth, slot size is increased over training, for example from 2 to 64. Early training stays close to local AR-like prediction; later training requires reconstruction of larger spans and encourages coarser-grained parallel generation. The paper also introduces ordered_sampling, where token-level masking importance increases from left to right within a slot, combined with 1/p_mask normalization so the model emphasizes getting early slot tokens right. That makes sense because early tokens anchor the rest of the span. Additional knobs such as grouped_noise, max_span_length, and noise_sorting support prefix completion, fill-in-the-prefix, fill-in-the-middle, and random-span masking. Relative to BD3-LMs, Zarya does not commit to a fixed block size. Relative to Eso-LMs, it is not only a loss-level fusion; it also redesigns sample structure and curriculum. Relative to ReFusion, it puts more emphasis on train-inference decoupling.2e:T7d7,From the full text provided, the experimental setup uses Qwen3-0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B backbones, fine-tuned for one epoch on a 32M-example instruction dataset totaling about 37.7B tokens, spanning math, coding, and general instruction following. Since masked tokens cannot attend to future masked tokens, the method may be learning structured span infilling rather than a fully order-free generation process. For pretraining relevance, the key issue is not a single benchmark win but whether the slot curriculum can scale to larger pretraining runs rather than only working in instruction continuation.30:Tace,ATC 的基本设定是，在输入和最终答案之间插入若干连续的 abstract thought token，但训练时并不给这些 token 任何人工语义标签，也不要求它们对应自然语言步骤。模型只对最终任务目标负责。关键做法不是“加 token”本身，而是围绕这些 token 设计一套逐级加难的课程。

课程的核心思想是，把原本难以直接学会的复杂任务拆成一串分布 D1, D2, ...，每一阶段都比上一阶段稍难，并且需要多一个 latent thought step 来承接更复杂的中间计算。模型先在较简单分布上学会利用较短的 thought chain；当达到阈值后，再进入更难阶段，增加问题复杂度和可用的 latent reasoning 深度。这样做的目的，是让后期阶段的某个 thought token 可以把前期阶段已经学到的表示当作“现成子程序”继续使用，而不是从头在最终监督下硬学长程组合计算。

理论部分聚焦 parity 任务，并回应 Lotfi 等人的 conjecture。作者分析一层 attention 模型在 ATC 下的梯度动力学，证明在一定条件下，一次足够大的梯度更新就会让注意力分数集中到最近的 thought token 上，从而出现所谓 attention simplicity bias：模型倾向于依赖最容易提供预测信号的中间 token。这个结果的意义不是 parity 本身，而是说明 curriculum 可以把原本 one-shot 难学的高阶函数，转化成一串局部可学的中间表示学习问题。

但作者也很诚实地指出，理论假设里“早期阶段学到的表示会被后续阶段保留”在实践中并不会自动成立。为此他们提出 curriculum backtracking：每推进到新阶段后，都重新在所有已完成阶段上评估；如果某个旧阶段准确率跌破阈值，就退回去继续训练，直到旧能力恢复。这个机制有点像显式的 retention control，目的是防止 latent thought 的语义漂移和灾难性遗忘。

另一个关键工程点是训练长 latent chain 的成本。若对所有 thought step 做完整反传，激活存储和计算量会随链长线性甚至更糟地增长。作者因此引入 truncated backpropagation through time，只在局部窗口内回传梯度，让更长的抽象思维链可训练。这里的取舍很明确：牺牲一部分全局梯度精确性，换取可扩展的链长和更稳定的训练。

与已有方法相比，ATC 不同于显式 scratchpad 监督，因为它不规定中间格式；也不同于单纯 curriculum learning，因为它不是只在输入难度上做排序，而是把课程和 latent thought depth 绑定起来；也不同于直接加 latent token 的做法，因为它额外处理了表示保留和训练成本这两个常见失败点。31:Tae8,ATC inserts continuous abstract thought tokens between the input and the final answer, but does not assign them any human-readable meaning and does not supervise them with target traces. The model is trained only on the end task. The key idea is not merely adding latent tokens; it is coupling them to a staged curriculum.

The curriculum defines a sequence of increasingly difficult distributions. At each stage, the task becomes slightly harder and the model is allowed or required to use one more latent thought step. The intention is that later stages can build on representations learned in earlier stages, effectively reusing prior thought tokens as intermediate subroutines. This turns a hard one-shot learning problem into a sequence of locally learnable representation-learning problems.

The theoretical analysis focuses on parity and addresses the conjecture from Lotfi et al. The authors study gradient dynamics in a one-layer attention model trained with ATC and show that, under suitable assumptions, a single sufficiently large gradient step can make attention concentrate on the most recent thought token. This formalizes the attention simplicity bias in this setting: the model prefers intermediate tokens that provide the easiest predictive signal. The point is not parity itself, but the mechanism by which curriculum can make otherwise hard high-degree functions learnable through staged latent computation.

The paper is careful about the gap between theory and practice. A key theoretical assumption is that representations learned in earlier curriculum phases remain intact and usable later. Empirically, this does not happen automatically. To address that, the authors introduce curriculum backtracking: after advancing to a new stage, the model is reevaluated on all previously completed stages, and if performance on an earlier stage drops below threshold, training returns to that stage until the capability is restored. This acts as an explicit retention mechanism against semantic drift and catastrophic forgetting in latent thoughts.

A second engineering contribution is truncated backpropagation through time for long latent chains. Full backprop across all thought steps makes activation storage and compute grow with chain length. Truncated BPTT limits gradient propagation to local windows, trading some gradient fidelity for tractable training of deeper latent reasoning chains.

Relative to prior work, ATC differs from explicit scratchpad supervision because it does not prescribe an intermediate format; from plain curriculum learning because it ties curriculum progression to latent reasoning depth; and from naive latent-token insertion because it explicitly handles representation retention and training cost, which are major practical failure modes.32:T85c,The experiments span theory-driven validation and three task families: parity, graph reasoning, and multi-digit arithmetic. The goal is not a single benchmark score, but to test whether ATC actually induces useful abstract thought tokens and whether those thoughts remain stable under curriculum progression.

On parity, used as a canonical hard-to-learn setting, direct training on the full target distribution struggles, whereas ATC substantially improves learning. The attention patterns also align better with the theory: later stages rely heavily on the most recent thought token, consistent with the predicted attention simplicity bias. The most informative evidence here is not just final accuracy, but the evolution of attention and learning trajectories across curriculum stages.

On graph tasks and multi-digit arithmetic, ATC outperforms fixed-difficulty training and other baselines in sample efficiency and final task performance. The ablations are especially important. Removing curriculum backtracking causes earlier-stage performance to degrade as the curriculum advances, showing that latent representations are indeed overwritten by later training. Removing truncated BPTT preserves fuller gradients in principle, but training cost rises quickly and chain length becomes hard to scale. With backtracking, the model maintains competence on earlier stages while extending the latent chain; with truncated BPTT, deeper latent reasoning becomes trainable under practical resource limits.

Three empirical lessons stand out. First, latent thoughts are not automatically useful; they need a staged training signal. Second, retention is central: without an explicit mechanism, longer curricula can erase the very intermediate representations they are supposed to build on. Third, the bottleneck in long latent reasoning is not only expressivity but also memory and optimization stability, so engineering choices are part of the method rather than implementation detail. At each step, the network emits a distribution for each writable position; the scheduler selects a group R based only on such per-position distributions; the sampler then draws each position in R independently. This abstraction covers absorbing-state masked diffusion, remasking diffusion, and the terminal phase of uniform-state diffusion. The main theoretical claims are sharp. If the positions in R are conditionally dependent given the frozen tokens, the divergence incurred by that step is at least the total correlation of the group. No set of per-position distributions can certify group independence, because two joint distributions may share identical one-position marginals while allowing different combinations of values. The states created by a dependent parallel write are also states where the standard per-position masked cross-entropy objective does not determine the needed joint conditionals. A further reachability result shows that simply writing one position at a time can also fail under hard constraints when the rest of the sequence pins a token. By definition, each symbol appears exactly once in every row and every column. Second, concentrating mixers into contiguous depth bands hurts performance. So the same set of mixers performs worse when grouped into blocks than when distributed throughout depth. That is an important result because many hybrid designs implicitly assume stage-wise specialization, such as local mechanisms early and global ones late.

The paper is more useful as an experimental design paper than as a single-model result paper.38:T5c4,RLPF proceeds in four stages. First, parameters are grouped by semantic role rather than matched tensor by tensor. The groups include patch embedding, sequence mixing, feed-forward blocks, and normalization. This is necessary because attention projections and SSM transition parameters are neither shape-compatible nor functionally identical. Second, each group is projected into a shared low-rank latent space. The geometric choice is treated as a design hyperparameter, not as evidence that raw weights intrinsically live on a manifold. Third, fusion is performed in that latent space with component-dependent geometry: some groups use Euclidean averaging, while others use a Lorentz-model hyperbolic barycenter, implemented as a Fréchet mean under squared geodesic distance. The paper also adds a geodesic anchor objective to regularize the fused point relative to branch-specific representations and reduce instability in curved space. Fourth, the fused latent codes are decoded back into a ViT branch and an SSM branch, and a small learned gate combines their logits. This is the key conceptual point: the method does not collapse two models into one unified parameterization. It uses geometry-aware initialization plus lightweight training to build a retained two-branch hybrid. Compared with model soups, task arithmetic, or TIES, the novelty is less about the averaging rule itself and more about defining a role-based cross-architecture correspondence before fusion.39:T449,The evaluation covers CIFAR-10, Oxford-IIIT Pet, and ImageNet-1K. The most useful aspect of the experimental design is that it separates several effects that are often conflated: ImageNet results before fine-tuning are reported separately from final fine-tuned gated-hybrid performance; Euclidean versus Lorentz fusion is compared; and the contribution of parameter grouping and gating is ablated. The qualitative takeaways are: (1) geometry-aware fusion provides a usable initialization, but most of the final gain appears to come from retaining both branches and fine-tuning them; (2) different parameter groups prefer different geometries, and the paper does not claim hyperbolic fusion is universally better; (3) the learned gate is important for stable combination of branch outputs. Each head’s query and key projection is constrained to St(d,r), the space of matrices with orthonormal columns. The optimizer projects the Euclidean gradient onto the Stiefel tangent space, accumulates a scalar second moment per frame using the Frobenius norm of the tangent gradient, applies a trust-region cap to the tangent step, retracts back to the manifold with a polar retraction, and transports momentum by projection after retraction. The scalar second moment removes per-coordinate adaptivity but preserves O(d) equivariance, so the update does not depend on an arbitrary coordinate system. The paper proves several properties of this update: steepest descent in the embedded metric, scale independence, better conditioning, and exact O(d) equivariance. A key mechanism result is that weight decay has zero Riemannian gradient on the Stiefel manifold because W lies in the normal space. This explains why Euclidean weight decay can damage attention geometry while the constrained update does not move along the manifold in response to that term. The paper also argues that the attention gauge is a joint O(r) action on WQ and WK, not separate Grassmann structure for each matrix; gauge directions carry no gradient, so gauge removal is not the main reason the method helps.3b:T4c1,The method uses block-level conditioning. A learned codebook defines a bounded set of block embeddings. A shared hypernetwork uses each code embedding to construct block parameters layer by layer by merging the underlying expert bases. Each constructed block therefore already contains information from the full expert pool. During token processing, a router selects only a small number of these blocks for each token. Participation is controlled by full-pool composition, execution is controlled by the number of selected blocks, and materialization is bounded by the codebook size.

The paper also introduces Dual-Path Residual Gating. Instead of merging expert bases into a single linear path, it composes separate value and gate paths and combines them through a gated product. This gives the composed expert a nonlinear dependence on expert bases without increasing the number of raw experts. Compared with sparse MoE, non-selected raw experts can still influence a token through block composition. Compared with dense MoE, the model avoids executing all experts per token. Compared with per-token or per-segment parameter merging, it avoids materializing a new expert-sized parameter set for every routing unit.3c:Tb27,技术主线有三步。

第一步，把 masked diffusion 的 tau-leaping sampler 重写成 ordered random partition 的等价形式。这个重写很关键，因为原始 CTMC/Gillespie 视角更接近逐坐标事件过程，不容易直接分析“某一步并行揭示一批坐标”带来的误差；而 partition 视角把整个采样轨迹表示成坐标集合被分成若干按顺序揭示的块，factorization error 就能自然写成对这些块内条件依赖的累积。

第二步，引入 dependence density ρ(u)。按论文描述，除去一个 N-1 的比例因子，ρ(u) 可以理解为：当其余坐标以概率 u 独立地已被揭示时，任意两个未揭示坐标之间平均 conditional mutual information 的密度。这个定义很有力，因为它把目标分布 π 的依赖结构压缩成一个一维函数。随后作者给出 ε_fact 的精确积分表示，schedule 的作用只通过权重项进入，而数据分布的全部难点都被放进 ρ(u)。这一步把“采样 schedule 优化”从一个离散、分布相关、难以下手的问题，变成了一个可分析的泛函优化问题。

第三步，分析不同依赖结构下的最优 schedule 形态。
- 对局部依赖分布，例如遍历马尔可夫链或足够规则的平稳过程，ρ_N 收敛到非退化连续 profile g。在这个 regime 下，优化平滑 schedule 只能改善 ε_fact 的前导常数，不能改变 N/K 的主阶，因此线性 schedule 是 order-optimal。这个结论很重要，因为它说明对很多“局部相关”的序列数据，花很多力气调花哨 schedule，收益可能只是常数级。
- 对 exchangeable mixtures 这类由全局 latent variable 诱导依赖的分布，ρ_N 会集中在原点附近，极限 profile 退化。此时早期揭示少量坐标能快速降低后续不确定性，因此 schedule 形状会显著影响误差阶。论文给出一个很强的例子：当 K_N≈log N 时，uniform schedule 的误差是 Ω(N/log N)，而 geometric schedule 可以做到 O(log N)。这不是常数差，而是阶的变化。

除此之外，论文还给出几个配套结果：有限步最优解满足的 stationarity equations；在大 N 极限下的变分问题及闭式 leading-order optimizer；以及 tau-leaping 中块大小随机性相对同极限 schedule 的 deterministic planner 所带来的额外 penalty。作者还把 total correlation 和 dual total correlation 也写成 ρ 的函数，从而把已有一些 heuristic 和上界放进同一框架里。

从方法取舍看，这篇工作没有去设计更复杂的联合块预测器，而是接受“仍用一维条件预测器”这一现实设定，转而优化采样 schedule。这样做的意义在于，它对应当前 masked discrete diffusion 最常见的实现路径，也更容易落地到现有 diffusion LM 系统里。3d:Tbae,The technical story has three main parts.

First, the paper rewrites the masked-diffusion tau-leaping sampler in an equivalent ordered-random-partition form. This is a useful reformulation. The original CTMC or Gillespie view is natural for exact one-coordinate-at-a-time simulation, but it is awkward for analyzing the error caused by revealing a whole block in parallel. The partition view makes the trajectory a sequence of revealed coordinate blocks, which is exactly the right object for expressing factorization error.

Second, the paper introduces the dependence density rho(u). Up to an N-1 scaling factor, rho(u) is the average conditional mutual information between two distinct coordinates when each of the remaining coordinates is independently revealed with probability u. This is the conceptual center of the paper. It compresses the dependence structure of the target distribution into a one-dimensional function. The authors then derive an exact integral representation of the factorization error epsilon_fact in which the schedule appears only through weighting terms, while all distribution-specific structure is captured by rho. This turns schedule optimization into a tractable functional problem.

Third, the paper analyzes optimal schedules under different dependence regimes.
- For locally dependent distributions, such as ergodic Markov chains or sufficiently regular stationary processes, rho_N converges to a nondegenerate continuous profile g. In this regime, optimizing over smooth schedules can improve only the leading constant of epsilon_fact, not its N/K scaling. So the linear schedule is order-optimal.
- For exchangeable mixtures, where dependence is global and mediated by a latent variable, rho_N concentrates near the origin and the limiting profile degenerates. In this regime, early fine-grained steps matter much more, because revealing a small number of coordinates can sharply reduce uncertainty about the latent structure. Here the schedule can change the asymptotic order of the error. The paper gives a striking example: when K_N is about log N, the uniform schedule has error Omega(N / log N), while a geometric schedule achieves O(log N).

The paper also derives stationarity equations for finite-step optimizers, a large-N variational problem with a closed-form leading-order optimizer, and an asymptotic penalty induced by the randomness of block sizes in tau-leaping relative to a deterministic planner with the same limiting schedule. It further expresses total correlation and dual total correlation through rho, which helps place several existing heuristics and bounds into one framework.

An important modeling choice is what the paper does not do. It does not introduce a more expensive joint block predictor. Instead, it accepts the practical setting of one-coordinate conditional predictors and optimizes the sampler around that constraint. That makes the analysis more relevant to current masked discrete diffusion implementations.3e:T5e7,The provided text indicates both theory and empirical validation, though the full numerical tables are not included in the excerpt. The main takeaways are clear.

1. The paper develops estimators for the dependence density rho, so the framework is not purely abstract. It aims to support practical schedule selection from data or samples.

2. On locally dependent distributions, the experiments should verify that linear schedules are already near-optimal and that schedule optimization mainly improves constants rather than scaling.

3. On exchangeable mixtures or other globally dependent distributions, the experiments should show that geometric schedules with finer early steps outperform uniform schedules substantially, matching the theoretical order separation. The headline asymptotic result stated in the text is that when K_N is about log N, the uniform schedule yields factorization error Omega(N / log N), whereas the geometric schedule yields O(log N).

4. Since the paper analyzes the penalty from random block sizes, any comparison against a deterministic planner is worth checking to see whether that asymptotic gap is already visible at practical sequence lengths.

The architecture has untied prelude and coda stacks, with a middle block of k layers reused for d recurrences, so parameter depth is p+k+l while realized compute depth is p+kd+l. The main experiments use a Huginn-style configuration such as (2, 4⊗32, 2).

To characterize instability, the authors define trace entropy, which measures uncertainty along the loop-wise reasoning trajectory for each token. Incorrect reasoning traces tend to have higher trace entropy. Using a logit-lens analysis, they then identify two token behaviors. Easy tokens improve monotonically across iterations, with growing top-1 vs top-2 margins. Hard tokens do not: they often become confident too early and then attempt revision later, or show unstable refinement patterns. These hard tokens account for only about 10%–15% of the reasoning trace but appear to be disproportionately important.

LoopCD builds on this observation. Standard contrastive decoding uses logits from an expert model and an amateur model. LoopCD replaces that external contrast with an internal one: logits from the final loop iteration serve as the refined distribution, while logits from earlier iterations provide the contrastive signal. The intuition is that later iterations are usually more refined, but earlier iterations may preserve useful intermediate evidence before unstable late-stage refinement distorts it. The final sampling distribution is formed by contrasting these loop-wise logits.

A practical advantage is that no extra model is needed and almost no extra forward cost is incurred, because the intermediate hidden states and logits are already produced during looping. The paper also argues that the gains are concentrated on hard tokens rather than spread uniformly across the sequence, which makes the method more targeted than generic decoding heuristics.41:T5e4,The paper evaluates LoopCD on arithmetic reasoning, code generation, and question answering, and reports consistent gains over standard decoding and stronger decoding baselines. First, trace entropy is strongly associated with reasoning quality. On GSM8K, incorrect reasoning traces show systematically higher entropy than correct ones, suggesting that loop instability leaves a measurable uncertainty signature.

Second, hard tokens are rare but important. They make up roughly 10%–15% of the reasoning trace, yet random replacement experiments in Table 1 show that perturbing hard tokens hurts accuracy much more than perturbing easy tokens. This is one of the strongest pieces of evidence in the paper because it moves beyond correlation and shows that these tokens are closer to the actual bottleneck.

Third, the gains from LoopCD are concentrated on hard tokens. The selective-intervention analysis in Section 5.4 indicates that applying the method to those tokens captures most of the benefit, while intervening on easy tokens yields much smaller returns. That supports the paper’s central mechanism.

Fourth, the method is computationally light. Unlike conventional contrastive decoding, it does not require an auxiliary amateur model. A focused skim should take about 20–30 minutes.43:T82e,The method, GravityOCR, is a parameter-shared AR–block-diffusion model built by adapting GLM-OCR. The same decoder is run under two attention patterns. The first path is a block-diffusion drafter. The output sequence is partitioned into contiguous blocks of size at most B. Dependencies remain causal across blocks, but attention is bidirectional within the current block. During training, a random subset of positions in the current block is masked and the model learns to denoise them conditioned on the completed prefix and the partially observed block. At inference, the current block starts fully masked and is iteratively denoised to produce a draft block in parallel.

The second path is a causal AR verifier. Given the same prefix, it checks the draft token by token and commits only the longest prefix that matches AR greedy predictions. Once a mismatch appears, commitment stops and the next drafting round begins. This design is the key idea: the diffusion path proposes, but the AR path decides. With top-1 verification, the committed output matches pure AR greedy decoding in exact arithmetic, so acceleration comes from accepting multiple drafted tokens per round rather than changing the final decision rule.

This differs from standard speculative decoding, which usually relies on a separate small drafter or an auxiliary multi-token head. Here both drafting and verification use the full shared backbone. Training combines the original AR NLL with a block-diffusion denoising objective so the model can operate under both masks. Post-training then applies GRPO only through the causal AR path using OCR rewards at the sequence and structure levels. The rationale is clean: optimize the path that determines the final output, and let shared parameters transfer improvements to the drafter indirectly. The paper also contrasts direct block-diffusion commitment with self-speculative verification. Direct commitment offers more parallelism but is brittle on tables, formulas, and other structurally coupled outputs; verification trades some parallelism for AR-like reliability.44:T69d,The model is evaluated on OmniDocBench v1.6 after adapting GLM-OCR. A solid skim should take about 20–30 minutes.46:T835,技术方案分两层。第一层是 selective absorption 机制。作者给每个位置加一个二值 absorption indicator；一旦某个位置被 absorb，它的 outgoing transition rate 置零，不再参与后续 CTMC 演化。这样就把原来“所有位置持续更新”的 uniform discrete flow，改成“部分位置冻结、其余位置继续流动”的混合过程。关键约束是：对仍然 active 的位置，保持原来的 uniform-flow velocity，不去改训练目标，也不重写 denoiser。

第二层是如何决定吸收顺序。随机吸收显然不行，因为一旦把错 token 固定住，就失去后续纠错机会。作者提出 LEDFlow，用 predictive entropy 做局部可靠性估计：每一步在给定 absorption budget 下，选当前熵最低的 active positions，把它们按当前最可能 token 固定下来；其余位置继续按 kinetic-optimal velocity 更新。下一步再重新计算熵，因此顺序是自适应的，而不是预先排好的静态 order。

理论部分的重点不是证明整个 sampler 全局最优，而是分析“不可逆吸收”引入的误差。作者把 stepwise absorption error 分解成两个 KL 项：一个对应被同时吸收位置之间的 joint dependence 丢失，另一个对应在已吸收上下文条件下的 conditional prediction error。随后在 oracle-reachable states 和 entropy-error regularity 的假设下，证明在固定吸收预算时，选择最低熵位置可以最小化 conditional error 上界。这个论证的意义在于解释为什么局部熵是合理信号，而不是仅凭经验有效。

作者还专门讨论了 global entropy lookahead。直觉上，往前看几步似乎能做更优决策，但论文指出在 denoiser 不完美时，未来状态估计误差会层层累积，decision error bound 会随 lookahead window 增长。也就是说，复杂的全局规划未必比局部熵更稳，反而更贵、更脆弱。这一点和很多生成式推理系统里的经验是相通的：如果模型本身有偏差，过深的 rollout 可能放大而不是消除误差。47:T89f,The method has two layers. The first is selective absorption. Each position is assigned a binary absorption indicator; once a position is absorbed, its outgoing transition rates are set to zero, so it no longer evolves under the CTMC. This changes the original all-positions-update regime of uniform discrete flow into a mixed process where some positions are frozen and others continue to move. A key design choice is that the velocity on active positions is left unchanged, so the method does not alter the trained denoiser or the underlying flow objective.

The second layer is the absorption policy. Randomly freezing positions is risky because an incorrect absorbed token cannot be corrected later. The proposed sampler, LEDFlow, uses predictive entropy as a local reliability signal. At each step, under a fixed absorption budget, it selects the active positions with the lowest entropy and absorbs them using their current most likely values. The remaining positions continue evolving under the kinetic-optimal velocity. Entropy is recomputed at every step, so the generation order is adaptive rather than predetermined.

The theory is framed around the error introduced by irreversible absorption. The authors decompose the stepwise absorption error into two KL terms: one for the loss of joint dependence among simultaneously absorbed positions, and one for conditional prediction error under the context created by previously absorbed values. Under assumptions on oracle-reachable states and entropy-error regularity, they show that, with a fixed absorption budget, choosing the lowest-entropy positions minimizes an upper bound on the conditional error term. This does not prove global optimality, but it gives a principled reason why local entropy is the right signal.

The paper also analyzes global entropy lookahead. In principle, evaluating future successor states could yield better decisions. In practice, with an imperfect denoiser, future-state estimation errors accumulate, and the decision-error bound grows with the lookahead window. The implication is important: more global planning is not necessarily more reliable, and can be both slower and less robust than a local entropy rule.48:T61d,The experiments span three task groups: structured reasoning, multimodal understanding, and text-to-image generation. The reasoning results are the most informative because they expose the exact failure mode the method is designed to fix.

In the Sudoku trajectory diagnostic, the native kinetic-optimal sampler produces 9.4% correct-to-wrong reversions, while LEDFlow reduces this to 2.6%. The fraction of token changes occurring after t = 0.75 also drops from 46% to 15%, which is a strong mechanistic result: the method is not just improving final accuracy, it is specifically suppressing unstable late revisions.

On Nikoli Sudoku, LEDFlow reaches 0.845 solve accuracy and achieves the best average rank across nine reasoning tasks. The pattern matters more than the single number: gains are largest on tasks with strong structural dependence, where late token flips are especially costly.

For text-to-image generation, LEDFlow achieves the best GenEval overall score among decode-time samplers, with a 2.8% absolute improvement over the native sampler. For multimodal understanding, it improves over the native sampler on all six reported benchmarks. The ablations are also useful. Entropy-guided absorption outperforms alternative absorption orders, supporting the central design choice. For lookahead, mean absolute score error rises from 0.17 with a single lookahead term to 1.76 under full lookahead, while longer lookahead can cost about 8x more inference time without meaningful gains. That empirical pattern lines up well with the theoretical analysis.49:T464,This is a skim paper, but it is worth a careful read if you work on diffusion LM, discrete flow, or any-order generation. The locked answer is then compared with the gold answer to decide whether it is correct or wrong. A key part of the analysis is a surface-matched protocol: correct and wrong lock-ins are paired so that observable statistics such as confidence, entropy, margin, and answer stability are closely balanced. This isolates the contribution of hidden states.

Second, they propose LOCKR, a lightweight test-time planner. LOCKR uses the observed hidden-state trajectory as the planning state. A trajectory-based risk detector decides whether to continue the current denoising path or enter repair. If repair is triggered, targeted remasking creates a fixed bank of local counterfactual branches. These branches are continued, scored by a trajectory-aware verifier, and a final selector chooses the retained continuation. Compared with full restart or uniform extra computation, LOCKR spends compute only on high-risk cases. First, the model uses a Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture. The encoder handles the causal prefill side, and decoder global KV is projected from the final encoder hidden states. 第一是 exactness。算法仍然保证最终输出分布与直接从 target model 自回归采样完全一致，不是近似采样。也就是说，加速不以分布偏移为代价。

从机制上看，Poisson process 在这里承担了两个角色：一是提供可解析的随机候选生成与耦合工具，二是提供天然适合 key-based watermark 的随机源。相比常见 token-level maximal coupling 或基于 exponential race 的构造，这种做法更适合扩展到 list 级别，并把“接受”和“嵌入信号”统一到同一随机过程里。51:T958,The main idea is a Poisson-process-based multi-draft speculative sampling algorithm. Standard speculative decoding usually uses one drafted continuation and lets the target verify it token by token. Here, the algorithm generates and verifies multiple draft continuations and uses Poisson processes to build an exact list coupling. The novelty is not merely having multiple drafts; it is that Poissonization gives a coupling structure with several desirable properties.

First, exactness. The final output distribution is exactly the same as direct autoregressive sampling from the target model. This is not an approximation scheme.

Second, drafter invariance. The paper emphasizes a list-coupling-without-communication construction, which makes the acceptance mechanism less tied to a particular drafter implementation. That matters even more under watermarking, because a watermark that depends too strongly on one drafter can be brittle and harder to analyze statistically.

Third, natural watermarkability. The watermark is not bolted on after speculative decoding. Instead, keyed randomness is embedded directly into the Poisson-process sampling procedure, producing a recoverable statistical signal while keeping the target law unbiased. The claimed benefit is that watermark strength does not deteriorate simply because sampling efficiency improves. In other words, the efficiency gain from multi-draft verification does not have to be paid for by weakening the watermark in the same way as in earlier impossibility-style results.

Fourth, the theoretical comparison point is Rowan et al. 2025. The authors claim a provably higher acceptance rate than that method. Importantly, they do not claim to invalidate the no-go theorem of Hu and Huang 2024. They explicitly state that the trade-off still applies for a fixed number of drafts. Their contribution is to improve the frontier by introducing the number of drafts as an additional degree of freedom.

Mechanistically, the Poisson process plays two roles: it provides an analyzable random mechanism for candidate generation and exact coupling, and it also provides a natural source of keyed randomness for watermarking. Compared with token-level maximal coupling or exponential-race-style constructions, this seems better suited to list-level coupling and to unifying acceptance and watermark embedding within one stochastic process.52:T676,The analysis starts from one linear layer, Y = XW^T. An invertible transformation P is inserted as Z = XP and V = WP^{-T}, preserving the full-precision output while changing the coordinates seen by activation and weight quantizers. Activation quantization is modeled as per-token symmetric uniform quantization with a dynamic scale determined by ||Z_t||_∞. For 4-bit activations, q_A = 2^{4-1}-1 = 7. The weight quantizer is left general; it may be standard rounding or an optimized method such as GPTQ.

The key result is an exact decomposition of the local weight-activation quantization error into an activation-guided weight compensation term and an orthogonal residual. The first term is the part that weight optimization can reduce along directions supported by the quantized activations. The second term is orthogonal to that compensatable subspace; once P is fixed, it cannot be removed by better weight compensation. This separates two roles that are often mixed together: weight optimization fits the output within a chosen coordinate system, while transformations change the residual structure before quantization.

The paper then analyzes the orthogonal residual to explain common design choices. Random orthogonal rotations reduce the impact of persistent channel-wise outliers on per-token quantization scales. Sign selection reduces unfavorable alignment between outlier structure and the rotation basis. Channel scaling balances activation-side and weight-side quantities. 第一步，语义聚合移到 pre-RoPE 空间。也就是先在未旋转的 Q/K 表示上做 block 级汇聚，得到更稳定的 block semantic summary。这样做的原因很直接：pre-RoPE 表示没有相位旋转，均值或其他简单聚合不会破坏高频分量，也不会把相邻 token 的局部顺序信息在池化时互相抵消。

第二步，几何信息不再依赖 pooled post-RoPE 向量隐式携带，而是通过离线 structural prior 重建。论文里给出的做法是根据相对 block 几何关系，预先构造一个相对位置偏置项，在推理时与在线语义分数相加，形成 closed-form routing score。这个设计的关键不是“加一个 bias”，而是把位置建模从在线 token 计算里拿掉，变成离线可缓存的结构先验，因此 routing 成本只和 block 数相关，不需要额外 token-level matching。

第三步，路由完全在 block 级进行。对每个 query block，依据 decoupled score 做 Top-p 或预算约束下的 block 选择，生成 causal block mask，再交给 Triton/block-masked attention kernel 执行。作者强调 routing function 的复杂度必须远低于 O(L^2)，否则 sparse attention 在实际 GPU 上未必比高优化的 dense FlashAttention 更快。

从区别上看，SGDR 和已有方法的分界很清楚。它不是像一些方法那样先粗筛 block 再做 token search，也不是在 post-RoPE pooled score 上做温度缩放或启发式修正，而是直接改写了 block score 的构造方式。理论上，它把“为什么 post-RoPE pooling 会坏掉”解释成高频相位干涉；工程上，它把补救从在线搜索换成离线先验，因此更适合长序列 prefill。56:T753,The method is Semantic-Geometric Decoupled Routing (SGDR). The central idea is to decompose block affinity into two parts: online semantic evidence and offline geometric bias. Existing methods implicitly mix both inside pooled post-RoPE features. SGDR separates them explicitly.

First, semantic aggregation is moved to pre-RoPE space. Query and key features are summarized at the block level before rotary rotation is applied. This avoids destructive interference from averaging rotated vectors, especially in high-frequency dimensions. The result is a more stable semantic summary for each block.

Second, positional structure is reconstructed separately rather than being expected to survive pooling. SGDR introduces an offline structural prior based on relative block geometry. At inference time, this prior is combined with the online semantic score to form a closed-form routing score. The important design choice here is that positional bias is no longer recovered through token-level computation or heuristic correction; it is encoded as a reusable block-level prior.

Third, routing remains fully block-level. For each query block, the router selects top blocks under a sparsity budget and produces a causal block mask, which is then consumed by custom Triton/block-masked attention kernels. This keeps routing cost well below quadratic complexity and avoids the common failure mode where sparse attention loses its advantage because routing itself becomes expensive.

Relative to prior work, SGDR is not a coarse-to-fine method with token refinement, and it is not a calibration trick on top of post-RoPE pooled scores. It changes the score construction itself. The theoretical claim is that post-RoPE pooling destroys useful information through phase cancellation; the engineering claim is that offline geometric priors are a better replacement than online search.57:T5c8,The evaluation covers long-context retrieval, understanding, language modeling, and video reasoning, with context lengths from 4K to 128K. Two results matter most.

First, SGDR stays close to exact full attention in accuracy across the tested range, and is better than or competitive with sparse baselines that depend on heuristic search or post-hoc compensation. The abstract does not list every task-level number, but the paper’s main empirical message is that fully block-level routing does not have to incur a large quality drop if the routing score is constructed correctly.

Second, the routing overhead is very small and remains stable as sequence length grows. The key number reported is that routing time stays below 3.4 ms across all evaluated lengths. At 128K, SGDR achieves a 5.03× speedup over FlashAttention. This is the result to pay attention to, because many sparse methods look attractive in asymptotic complexity but lose in wall-clock time once routing/search overhead is included.

The most informative ablations are likely the following: pre-RoPE vs post-RoPE pooling, to validate the phase-cancellation hypothesis; removing the geometric prior, to show that semantic pooling alone is insufficient; and varying block size or sparsity budget, to expose the quality/latency trade-off. At those states, the same model proposes multiple continuations using a higher proposal temperature. An LLM judge labels continuations as progress-making or non-progress-making. After the source processes a 4,096-token prefix, the receiver starts from the real next token and is evaluated on the following teacher-forced targets, with no target-side replay of the historical prefix. Attention KV is translated with ridge maps per layer, head, and role; keys are de-rotated before mapping and re-rotated for the target. Recurrent and convolution states are either directly reused or mapped with learned ridge-style translators. A factorial component experiment tests direct versus translated choices for K, R, and C. The selected base configuration translates KV but directly reuses both GDN components. A small identity-anchored correction is then trained with both language models frozen, using full-vocabulary KL from native 9B behavior to the handoff behavior plus an identity penalty. The trainable correction has 434,176 parameters.5e:T87f,The proposed method, QuantWM, is a training-free 2-bit KV-cache quantization framework. Its goal is not merely to reduce Key/Value reconstruction error, but to explicitly preserve attention logits and temporal consistency. It builds on the centroid-residual representation used in QVG: each Key is assigned to a BF16 centroid, and only the residual is quantized to low bitwidth. The paper argues that QVG is limited because centroid selection is driven mainly by K-means geometry, which optimizes feature-space distance rather than downstream impact on QK^T.

The first component is QSAC, quantization-sensitivity-aware clustering. Instead of selecting centroids purely by Key-space clustering quality, QSAC jointly considers Query sensitivity and residual dynamic range, aiming to reduce the effect of INT2 residual quantization on attention logits. Intuitively, some Key directions may have small Euclidean error but still be highly dangerous if they align with Query-sensitive directions and alter token ranking. QSAC tries to avoid such residual structures already at the clustering stage.

The second component is PSAC, principal-subspace attention compensation. Even with better clustering, Key quantization error can still be amplified along dominant Query directions and distort logits. PSAC extracts the principal Query subspace and uses low-rank projections to represent and compensate the Key error components along those sensitive directions during inference. The idea is not to fully reconstruct Keys, which is unrealistic at 2 bits, but to correct the error components that matter most for attention allocation. This is a different philosophy from simply increasing quantization fidelity: it accepts that full preservation is impossible and spends the available budget on the subspace that most affects retrieval behavior.

The overall design is coherent: QSAC makes Keys more quantization-friendly before compression, and PSAC compensates the most harmful attention shifts after compression. Because the method is training-free, it is intended as a practical drop-in replacement for existing KV-cache compression pipelines in video generation and world models.5f:T53a,The experiments cover several representative models, including LingBot-World-v2, Matrix-Game-2, LongCat-Video, HY-World 1.5, and Causal-Forcing, which suggests the authors are aiming for architecture-agnostic evidence rather than a single-model result. The headline outcome is that QuantWM substantially reduces temporal flickering, blur, and artifacts under 2-bit KV quantization while maintaining strong benchmark performance on metrics such as VBench. It also achieves up to 6.20x KV-cache memory compression with limited inference overhead.

The most important evidence comes from the diagnostic ablations. The paper separates Key-only and Value-only quantization and shows that most degradation comes from Keys. It then compares reconstruction errors and finds that Keys can have smaller numerical error than Values despite causing worse output quality. That result supports the paper's central claim: KV quantization should not be judged mainly by reconstruction magnitude, but by its effect on attention logits and token ranking. The method components are built directly around that diagnosis. Even without all table values in the provided text, the experimental story is clear: the goal is not just to preserve benchmark scores, but to fix temporal-consistency failures that benchmarks under-measure but humans notice immediately.60:T6ef,DPara 的关键做法是把 DSpark-style drafter 拆成“重的 diffusion backbone”和“轻的 autoregressive head”。在 target model 正在 verify 当前 draft 时，DPara 不去猜最终 accepted prefix 和 bonus token，而是让 diffusion backbone 为所有可能的 acceptance boundary 预先计算 draft representations，并且暂时不绑定 bonus token。等 verification 结果返回后，真实的 accepted boundary 和 bonus token 已经确定，再由轻量 AR head 把这些信息接进去生成下一轮可用 draft。这样，概率性错误不再导致 backbone fallback；只要 backbone 能在 target verification window 内跑完，backbone 延迟就被完全隐藏，关键路径上只剩 AR head。

标准 DFlash 并不能直接满足这个使用方式，因为它通常依赖单个带有上下文 feature 的 anchor，而 DPara 需要同时覆盖多个 acceptance boundary，并从 feature-less anchors 预测。论文因此提出 M-DFlash：从公开 DSpark checkpoint 初始化，只 finetune diffusion backbone，让它适配 multiple-anchor、feature-less 的输入 regime；AR head 保持冻结，不引入新的可训练参数。这一点很重要，因为它说明 DPara 不是重新训练一个完整 drafter，而是用较小代价把已有 DSpark-style drafter 改造成适合并行排程的版本。

与 SSD/PEARL 这类方法相比，DPara 的差别不在于“更会猜 outcome”，而是不再把 overlap 建立在猜测 outcome 上。与普通 DSpark 相比，DPara 保留了 parallel drafter 的 acceptance 能力，同时把最重的 backbone 从串行 draft-verify 路径里拿掉。代价是需要为多个 boundary 准备 backbone 输出，并要求额外 drafting 设备或足够的同机资源来保证 overlap window。61:T68a,DPara exploits the internal structure of a DSpark-style drafter: a heavy diffusion backbone followed by a lightweight autoregressive head. While the target model verifies the current speculative block, DPara runs the diffusion backbone ahead of time for every possible acceptance boundary and leaves the bonus token unspecified. Once verification completes, the true accepted boundary and bonus token are known; the lightweight AR head then conditions on that outcome and produces the next draft tokens. As long as the backbone finishes within the target verification window, the dominant part of drafting latency is hidden, and only the AR head remains on the critical path.

A standard DFlash backbone is not directly suitable for this schedule. In the serial setting, it anchors prediction on a single token after a fully featured prefix. DPara needs predictions from multiple feature-less anchors, one for each possible acceptance boundary. The paper introduces M-DFlash by initializing from a published DSpark checkpoint and finetuning only the diffusion backbone for this multiple-anchor, feature-less regime. The AR head is kept frozen, and no new trainable parameters are added.

The key difference from SSD or PEARL is that DPara does not try to make a better guess about the accepted prefix or bonus token. It removes the need for that guess. The key difference from serial DSpark is that DPara keeps the strong parallel drafter but moves the expensive backbone computation out of the serial draft-verify path. The cost is extra boundary coverage work and a requirement that drafting resources be provisioned well enough to complete inside the verification window.62:T4d5,The evaluation uses Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B on math, coding, and chat benchmarks. DPara outperforms the baselines on every model-dataset pair. Average speedups over autoregressive decoding are 3.21× for Qwen3-8B and 3.52× for Qwen3-14B, with a maximum reported speedup of 4.53×. Compared with DSpark, the strongest serial drafter, average gains are 11.1% and 5.1%. On Qwen3-14B, DPara improves average speedup over PEARL and SSD by 31% and 64%, respectively.

The batching results are central. DPara remains ahead of DSpark from batch size 1 to 16 and keeps more than 2× AR throughput at batch size 16. Outcome-dependent methods such as SSD degrade more sharply as batch size increases because a mismatch in any request can push the batch back to serial execution.

The resource studies are also informative. DPara-A10 preserves 98% of DPara's speedup while reducing drafting-device cost by about 90%. DPara-single preserves roughly 90%–95% of the speedup at small batch sizes. An ablation shows that finetuning only the diffusion backbone increases average acceptance length by 30.7%, which supports the claim that the multiple-anchor feature-less regime needs adaptation rather than a direct reuse of the original DFlash backbone.63:T47e,Read the introduction and Figures 1–2 first. The main point is the critical path, not the acceptance-rejection math.

Focus on why bonus-token conditioning is deferred to the AR head, and why the system covers all acceptance boundaries instead of predicting a single likely boundary. It first builds a merge set from a general corpus by collecting frequent contiguous n-grams of length 2 to 4. At inference time, merge candidates are selected with a longest-match rule when spans overlap. For each selected span, UMIM takes the static token embeddings and uses a lightweight single-layer attention module to produce one surrogate embedding, which replaces the original multi-token embeddings at the input layer.

The merge module is trained with predictive distillation. The pretrained LM is frozen, and only the merge module is updated so that the next-token distribution under compressed inputs matches the distribution under the original uncompressed sequence. The context-independent design makes the module reusable, but it is also a limitation: the same n-gram receives the same surrogate wherever it appears, which may be brittle for ambiguous phrases or spans whose role depends strongly on surrounding context. The method is applied to both prompt compression and autoregressive decoding context compression, with rollback used to replace multi-token KV-cache entries by single-step surrogate states.65:T407,F²DR evaluates DeepSearch along three axes. The Content axis checks whether retrieved information covers key knowledge points and is factually grounded. The Trajectory axis evaluates the search process, including intent understanding, search atomicity, planning consistency, gap resolution, planning comprehensiveness, and iterative novelty, while penalizing redundant reasoning and plan-execution mismatch. The Answer axis combines subjective criteria such as intent match, coherence, and conciseness with objective coverage of core information.
